name: How do I add more storage without changing the footprint?

mainEntity.name: How do I add more storage in a kitchen layout change without expanding the footprint?
mainEntity.text: How do I add more storage in a kitchen layout change without expanding the footprint?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen does not need a larger footprint to feel more functional. Often the better answer is to redesign the storage strategy. Taller upper cabinets, deep drawers, pull-outs, tray storage, corner solutions, and a properly designed pantry can dramatically improve capacity. In many kitchens, poor storage comes from wasted vertical space, awkward corners, or cabinet styles that look nice but do not hold much. Layout changes can also create hidden storage by shifting appliances, eliminating dead zones, or reworking an island or peninsula to serve multiple roles. The important part is to store items where they are actually used. Pots should be near the cooking zone, dishes near the dishwasher, and daily items in easy reach. Smart storage planning often delivers more day-to-day value than adding square footage. It also helps the kitchen feel cleaner because clutter has a place to go.
acceptedAnswer.description: More storage can often be added by using taller cabinets, deeper drawers, corner solutions, pantry units, and better appliance placement. A layout change does not always need more square footage; it often needs smarter use of vertical and hidden storage space.
